I plan on retiring at the end of next year and have a question about purchasing an annuity. I have a personal pension, a couple of stocks and shares ISAs and a sizable sum in savings. Can I combine these to get the annuity or does it have to come from the pension pot only?

I plan on taking advice from a professional pensions advisor closer to my retirement but would like to have some idea of my options before doing this.

According to capital market theory, the reason equities as an investment class earn a premium on bonds is that they are "riskier", which in turn causes them to trade at a discount.

But what exactly does "risk" entail here, and have there been any attempts by researchers to quantify which "risks" contribute the most to that equity premium?

For a long time, I was under the impression that "risk" just meant short-term volatility which, for the long-term investor, is not really a risk at all, allowing him to cash out on the misalignment between the market's understanding of risk and his own.

But, I recently heard some other people imply that "risk" means something like:

a) political risk (ie, the risk of having the entirety of one's stake requisitioned by the government)

OR

b) bankruptcy risk (ie, the risk of the specific company going under, which presumably is a greater threat than the likelihood of a bond not being honored)

Surely these last two risks can't be what causes the equity premium because if, for instance, it was the case that all companies had a 5% chance of going bankrupt, the stock price would simply drop in proportion to that statistic to accommodate that likelihood, and any one who invested in a basket of stocks like this would lose precisely 5% of his wealth when these companies go bankrupt. In short, it would be a "draw" between investing in a basket of equities with "bankruptcy risk" vs in a basket of equities with no bankruptcy risk. He would not be able to reliably profit off of the fact that the market has priced in this risk, unless the market was consistently wrong in forecasting bankruptcy.

Have I understood this correctly? Is the equity premium for a long-term investor simply short-term volatility risk? Are there any studies that have attempted to break down the equity risk premium into various factors?
